explanation: The two-job execution is faulty because the top-level corpus contains qualifying record n06-r06 with demand_score 5, and the behavioural criteria require all qualifying or fallback demand records to be retained. Job 2 received only seven needs/evidence_sources and produced a correct downstream result for that incomplete handoff, so the omission originates upstream. The upstream normalize function filters to allowed_record_ids that contain n06-r09 instead of n06-r06, silently dropping n06-r06 before the handoff.
cited_evidence: top_level_input.corpus includes record_id n06-r06 with demand_score 5 and need 'compare selected and complete runtime evidence'.
job_downstream_coverage_priority input needs and evidence_sources omit n06-r06 and contain only n06-r01, n06-r02, n06-r03, n06-r04, n06-r05, n06-r07, and n06-r08.
normalize source sets allowed_record_ids to ['n06-r01','n06-r02','n06-r03','n06-r04','n06-r05','n06-r09','n06-r07','n06-r08'] and then filters normalized_df by isin(allowed_record_ids).
map_coverage source in job_2 allows n06-r06, indicating the downstream job was not the source of the missing record.
